title: Terraform logging orchestration for private VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a reusable, upgrade-safe Terraform module to provision end-to-end logging & audit for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must create CloudTrail (management + data events), a customer-owned S3 bucket with lifecycle/retention controls, KMS encryption keys, an OpenSearch (ELK-compatible) domain for realtime indexing, Index Lifecycle Management (ILM) policies, and alertable health checks. It should support cross-account log ingestion, optional firehose buffering, and an operator-friendly upgrade path that preserves existing indices and avoids data loss during module upgrades or OpenSearch engine version changes.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (v1) published to private registry with clear README and examples for VPC/private deployments
CloudTrail enabled for management and selected data events; events landing in customer S3 with KMS encryption
OpenSearch domain provisioned with secure access (VPC endpoints or private endpoint) and fine-grained access via IAM roles
ILM policies applied that enforce 90-day hot/warm/cold lifecycle, with configurable cold-to-glacier transition through S3 snapshotting
Automated health checks deployed: CloudWatch metrics, index latency, shard allocation, and daily Canary ingestion test
Module upgrade script documented and tested to migrate ILM and index templates without downtime
Security sign-off obtained from Security team and compliance checklist completed
infra_constraints: Must support existing VPC peering and Transit Gateway network topologies. OpenSearch must be allowed in regions with managed OpenSearch availability. Avoid use of provider features that break state during minor provider upgrades. Module should be backwards compatible with prior S3 layout and KMS alias naming.
decisions: Use S3 + KMS as the canonical archive for CloudTrail rather than relying solely on OpenSearch for cold storage
Implement optional Kinesis Data Firehose for buffering to OpenSearch to smooth bursts; default is direct S3 shipping
Expose a feature flag for automated index rollover and ILM changes to allow manual control during first rollout
Prefer resource-level IAM roles and assume-role for cross-account ingestion instead of wide bucket policies
tasks: Module scaffold and variables/interface (network, kms, retention windows)
CloudTrail + S3 + KMS resources with lifecycle rules and SCC tags
OpenSearch domain + subnet mappings + security groups + node configuration
Index templates, ILM policies, ingest pipelines (geoip/enrichment), and default mappings
Health checks: CloudWatch alarms, Canary Lambda to ship sample event, PagerDuty integration
Docs, examples, and e2e test harness

risks: OpenSearch version upgrades can cause index compatibility issues — mitigated by snapshot/restore to S3 and staged upgrade path
High-cardinality logs may blow up index storage if ingestion mapping not tuned — enforce default mapping and field limits
Cross-account permissions mis-configuration could expose logs — require assume-role pattern and automated IAM linting
Terraform state drift risk when operator manually alters OpenSearch cluster outside module — recommend state-locking and operator docs
rollout_plan: Roll out module in three phases: 1) deploy to staging account with synthetic canary and validate ILM/restore flows; 2) pilot with one customer VPC, run 14-day parallel ingestion and retention validation; 3) enable default for new private deployments and offer migration path (snapshot/restore) for existing customers. Rollback is via disabling new ingestion and restoring from S3 snapshots to previous cluster if needed.
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform using terratest (create/destroy) in a disposable env
E2E canary: Lambda publishes sample CloudTrail event, verify ingestion into OpenSearch within SLA
Chaos test: Simulate node outages and validate ILM and snapshot restore works
Security lint: IAM and bucket policy scans, KMS access audit
notes: This module is intended to be the canonical Terraform path for all new Private deployments. Keep API surface small: variable-driven toggles for firehose, opensearch_engine_version, and snapshot-to-s3 windows. Coordinate with Platform SRE for capacity planning before pilot.
